title: Chapter 91: Increasing Popularity
html:
Chen Ge sighed with relief as he read the mission-completion message. The two-star Trial Mission had been easier than expected, probably because the spirits of Mu Yang High School meant him no harm.

Halfway through the mission, he had realized that the school’s inhabitants were not malevolent specters. Even the Pen Spirit bore no true malice. What happened to Fan Yu’s father had simply been karma.

The classroom and the deep well had unquestionably been the hardest side missions. He had yet to uncover the Sealed Classroom’s true secret; he had entered it only once, and fortunately, its spirits had let him leave. The Deep Well mission had been just as demanding. Even with police assistance, they had needed the entire night to find the well before dawn. Alone, he would certainly have failed.

Still, he was satisfied with the rewards. The hidden item did not excite him much. Legend claimed that Pen Spirits could predict the future, but his seemed both ignorant and utterly devoid of principles.

The night-long rain finally stopped. After praising Chen Ge’s contribution and taking his statement, the police drove him home. The emergency call and hours of digging had exhausted them; the officer beside him kept nodding off. Chen Ge edged toward the door to give the man more room. The rest of the journey passed in silence.

Chen Ge reached New Century Park at six. Whether from his Yin Yang Vision or his constant exposure to spirits, a deep chill had settled into him. He lay down but could not sleep. When he checked his phone, he found more than ten missed calls and unread messages.

Most of them came from He San, mainly asking about his safety and whether he needed to call the police. At the bottom of the inbox was a message from Doctor Gao. The good doctor said that Fan Yu’s symptoms might be related to the people around him, and he advised Chen Ge to pay closer attention to such individuals in the boy’s life.

The message was sent at 12:30 am. By then, Fan Yu’s aunt had come clean to Chen Ge. After replying to both He San and Doctor Gao, Chen Ge opened the video-sharing app and clicked into his personal page.

A four-hour livestream but not a word with the chat, and I even closed the stream several times in the middle without warning. I can only imagine the damage that was done to my popularity.

After detaining Fan Yu’s aunt, Chen Ge had ended the livestream to protect the boy’s privacy and future. With his attention needed elsewhere, he had given the viewers no explanation.

The main page loaded. One glance at the screen left him stunned: his follower count had climbed to 39,000.

I remember, before the livestream, I had less than 10,000 followers. What happened last night during the livestream?

Consumed by the side missions, he had simply let the stream run. He had expected little from it, making the sudden windfall all the more surprising.

As he tried to work out what had happened, He San called. Commotion filled the background when Chen Ge answered. “Boss! I knew you were still alive!”

Chen Ge ignored He San’s celebration and asked directly, “What happened last night during my livestream? Why did my followers and views grow so tremendously?”

“Your numbers were growing from the moment you started streaming, but slowly. Then you played the Pen Spirit game. Someone posted a thread on the app’s forum exposing Qin Guang’s plagiarism and linked your first livestream.” Indignation sharpened He San’s voice. “Qin Guang copied everything—the analysis, the setting, even the killer’s identity, except he used an actor! The proof was right in front of them, but his fans refused to admit it. They flooded the thread and claimed you were copying their idol.”

“Probably just paid trolls. Nothing unusual. What happened next?”

“People went to Qin Guang’s stream demanding an explanation, but he pretended not to notice. He even banned anyone who mentioned you. Still, the platform promoted him so heavily that he started with 800,000 viewers. The chat moved too fast for his team to catch every mention, and some curious viewers found their way to your stream.” He San grew more excited. “You peaked at 50,000 viewers—a mix of passersby, paid accounts, Qin Guang’s fans, and your own. Total chaos! You don’t have moderators, so the chat kept going for half an hour after the stream ended. All that activity pushed you onto the midnight Popular Ranking. Congratulations! Very few new hosts make it there so early.”

Chen Ge could imagine the previous night’s chaos, but it had been a blessing in disguise. His follower count had soared, and exposure—not content—was what he lacked.

“Slow down. After all, that was just my second livestream.” Chen Ge talked for a few more minutes with He San before hanging up.

He checked his private messages. Most contained insults, though a few users who resented Qin Guang’s bullying had written to support him.

Near the bottom of the inbox, Chen Ge recognized a familiar username. Its profile picture resembled the studio that had harassed him before. The message warned him against using dirty tricks and threatened to drive him off the platform.

Another host might have been frightened, but streaming and short videos were merely advertising for Chen Ge’s Haunted House. He blocked the account, closed the app, and picked up the black phone.

“Mu Yang High School (Scream Factor: 2 Stars): Scenario construction is complete. You may now visit it on the underground level.

“Warning: Mu Yang High School is part of the four-star scenario School of the Afterlife and occupies twice the space of a normal scenario. Please familiarize yourself with its layout before opening it to visitors.”

After reading the message, Chen Ge sat upright. Twice the size of a normal scenario? Wait… don’t tell me they moved the whole of Mu Yang High School here.

He put on his shoes and ran to the first floor, peeled off the wooden boards, and peered downward.

The abandoned underground parking lot had been transformed. Scorch marks blackened the stairs. Unfinished test papers littered a dark corridor, classroom doors creaked in the gloom, and shadows flitted among overturned desks.
